title: Middle-Class Surge
description: The global middle class is expanding significantly, with China and India poised to dominate by 2030. China's middle class has grown from 3% in 2001 to a projected majority by 2030, contributing to 17% of global GDP. Meanwhile, the middle class in the US earns between $45,000 and $135,000 annually, highlighting different economic scales.

representative_facts.fact_content: Over 70% of China’s population could be middle class by 2030
China and India will represent roughly two-thirds of the global middle-class population by 2030
A middle-income-three-member-household in the US earns about US$45,000 to US$135,000

title: Demographic Dynamics
description: The middle class population is a significant demographic in both the United States and China. In the US, 52% of the population was classified as middle class in 2016, with 92 million adults identified as part of this group. In China, a substantial shift occurred between 2001 and 2011, with 203 million people crossing the middle-income threshold. This highlights the growing economic power and changing income dynamics in these countries.

92 million middle class adults are Americans
203 million people in China crossed the middle-income threshold of $10 per day from 2001 to 2011

title: Global Consumption
description: The global middle class comprises 664 million adults, with 15% of the world's adult population belonging to this group. China plays a significant role, with 110 million middle-class adults and a potential consumption of nearly $10 trillion by 2030. The middle-class consumption worldwide is projected to reach $64 trillion by 2030.

representative_facts.fact_content: 664 million adults are part of the middle class this year
110 million middle class adults are Chinese
Middle-class consumption is expected to tally $64 trillion by 2030

title: Income Expansion
description: By 2030, China is projected to have around 400 million households with upper-middle and higher incomes, indicating significant economic growth. In 2011, 16% of the global population lived on $20 or more daily, reflecting a substantial portion of the world achieving a middle-class income level.

representative_facts.fact_content: China may have 400 million upper-middle income households by 2030
16% of global population lived on $20+ daily in 2011

title: Wealth Accumulation
description: China's economic landscape is rapidly evolving, with a significant increase in the number of millionaires and a burgeoning middle class. The number of millionaires in China is projected to double by 2025, reflecting the country's growing wealth. Additionally, middle-class consumption is anticipated to reach $64 trillion by 2030, highlighting the expanding economic power of this demographic. In 2000, only 3% of China's population was considered middle class, indicating substantial growth over the years.

representative_facts.fact_content: China's millionaires may double to 10 million by 2025
Middle-class consumption expected to hit $64 trillion by 2030
3% of China's population was middle class in 2000

title: Regional Shifts
description: Between 2001 and 2011, Asia and the South Pacific saw a significant rise in their share of the global middle-income population, increasing from 31% to 51%. China's middle-income population alone represented 30% of the global middle-income demographic by 2011. During the same period, China's poverty rate dropped from 41% to 12%, indicating substantial economic progress.

representative_facts.fact_content: Asia & South Pacific's middle-income share rose from 31% in 2001 to 51% in 2011
China's middle-income population was 30% of the global total in 2011
China's poverty rate fell from 41% in 2001 to 12% in 2011

title: Income Transition
description: In 2011, China's middle-income population reached 235 million, representing 18% of its total population. During the decade from 2001 to 2011, 356 million people in China transitioned out of poverty. In contrast, in 2001, North America's middle-income population was 10%, with a high-income population share of 43%.
